Rationale: Protecting property during an extreme rain event becomes significantly more challenging when a power outage occurs, as many critical home systems rely on electricity. One of the biggest concerns is basement and property flooding due to sump pump failure. Sump pumps are essential in keeping water from accumulating in basements and crawl spaces, but without power, they stop working, allowing floodwaters to rise unchecked. This can lead to extensive property damage, mold growth, and structural weakening. Homeowners can mitigate this risk by installing battery-powered or water-powered backup sump pumps, which can operate even when the main power supply is down. Beyond sump pump failure, power outages also impact other flood prevention measures, such as drainage systems and stormwater management infrastructure. Electrically powered drainage systems in urban areas may stop functioning, leading to street flooding that can spread to homes and businesses. Additionally, without power, residents may not receive timely weather alerts or emergency notifications, reducing their ability to take preventive action. To increase resiliency, communities should invest in stormwater infrastructure improvements, such as permeable pavement, improved drainage channels, and emergency flood barriers, while also ensuring backup power sources for critical flood management systems. At the individual level, homeowners should take proactive measures to safeguard their property before an extreme rain event occurs. This includes sealing foundation cracks, elevating valuable 45 items and electrical appliances in basements, and ensuring gutters and downspouts are clear of debris to direct water away from the home. Sandbags and water-absorbing barriers can provide additional protection in flood-prone areas. Having a home emergency kit that includes flashlights, portable power banks, and a battery-powered weather radio can help individuals stay informed and prepared during prolonged outages. On a community scale, collaboration is key to improving flood resilience. Local governments and emergency management agencies should work with residents to establish flood response plans and distribute resources such as sandbags and emergency sump pump backups before major storms. Investing in microgrids and community-based energy resilience programs can help ensure that essential services, including flood prevention systems, remain operational during outages.
